positions.name: MandateToEraseKnowledge
positions.frame: what authority is the speaker claiming when directing that knowledge be forgotten or removed?
positions.why: Both expressions are bare imperatives issued by the same actor in the same breath, each commanding the recipient to purge specific held knowledge (a fleet/contracts, then routes) rather than arguing a position about them. The relational and power reads both mark this pair as authority-ranking / coercive-pressure — the imperative form itself is the move, not persuasion. There is a small register difference (src-1 carries formal, protocol-flavored diction like 'procurement contracts'; src-2 is flatly instrumental) but both land at 'decision' conviction as settled, expected-to-be-executed instructions, so the pair coheres under a single directional read: an assertion of authority to compel erasure, expressed twice at slightly different registers.
